summary: Inyoung Chung works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, and Paris-Sorbonne University, as well as under Mircea Eliade (~1976–1986). He held posts at the University of Groningen (1976–1986) and University of Chicago Divinity School (1986–1991).
Iona Macgregor works in Indology. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).
Ippei Okamoto works in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Toyo University (attested 2014) and Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He was Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955).

Irawati Karve (1905–1970) worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and related fields. She studied at Huzurpaga, Fergusson College, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She served at Deccan College as Professor of Sociology and Anthropology (~1939–1970) and at the University of Pennsylvania (~1951–1952).

Irfan Habib (born 1931) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953), and New College (~1954–1957), and he worked as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1953.

Irving Babbitt (1865–1933) was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He studied at Williams College, Harvard College, the University of Paris, and Harvard University. He taught at Williams College (~1893–1894) and Harvard University (~1894–1933).

Isaac Schapera (1905–2003) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Cándido Candi, the University of Cape Town, and the London School of Economics, and held posts at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, and LSE (~1950–1969).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at the University of Rostock. He served at the Russian Bible Society and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a scholar of Tibetology. She studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Tibet University, EPHE, and Harvard, under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert, and taught anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).

Isabelle Ratié (born 1976) specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).
Isaiah Berlin (1909–1997) was a philosopher who studied at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932). He held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 until 1997.

Isaline Blew Horner (1896–1981) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held librarian and governing roles at Newnham and Cambridge, and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society.
Isao Nishitani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He has held posts at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She has held posts as a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo (attested 2016) and as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo (attested 2016).

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820–1891) studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, he held posts at Fort William College, Sanskrit College, and served as Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1851).

Iso Kern (born 1937) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Louvain, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University, and held academic posts at KU Leuven, Heidelberg University, Zurich, Fribourg, and the University of Bern.
Issaien Ikeyama works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1976) and Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).
Issei Suzuki (1863–1943) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and later served there as a professor.
